subject.title: Feature: Silence Watchdog + Response Delivery Confirmation — runtime-enforced operator visibility

question: Should OpenClaw implement one combined default operator-visibility contract for silence beacons plus final delivery confirmation, or sequence the work through narrower delivery-status and watchdog contracts first?
rationale: The request changes default channel-visible behavior, retry and duplicate-suppression semantics, no-response alerts, and per-channel configuration, which source inspection cannot safely choose without maintainer product intent.

options.title: Sequence Narrow Contracts First
options.body: Keep #47591 open as umbrella context while #87561/#46830 define delivery semantics and #77771 defines watchdog policy before implementation.

options.title: Sponsor Combined Core Feature
options.body: Approve one broad core feature and require explicit defaults, config migration posture, duplicate-suppression semantics, and live-channel proof before coding.

options.title: Decline Default Beacons
options.body: Keep explicit progress and heartbeat behavior opt-in or plugin/channel-owned if default generic status messages are too noisy.

recommendation.title: Sequence Narrow Contracts First
recommendation.body: Keep #47591 open as umbrella context while #87561/#46830 define delivery semantics and #77771 defines watchdog policy before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The broad decision spans shared outbound delivery, reply runtime, and session behavior where this history trail is strongest.
